study type: Case study and experimental (in vitro and animal) research
exposure: de novo CTR9 non-synonymous variants (p.(Glu15Asp) and p.(Pro25Arg))
human CTR9 mutants introduced into ctr9-knockout zebrafish
overexpression of human CTR9 mutant mRNA
outcome: stronger affinities to the PAF1 protein
cohort: The study included two unrelated human patients with macrocephaly, motor delay, and intellectual disability, along with zebrafish models for functional analyses.
finding: The two missense variants in CTR9 (p.(Glu15Asp) and p.(Pro25Arg)) cause a new syndrome involving macrocephaly, motor delay, and intellectual disability by disrupting CTR9 function and interfering with the normal intrinsic CTR9 function of the contralateral allele.
